title: ❌ MISDIAGNOSED — The key was never corrupted with trailing `}`. P0 APPEND-ONLY MEMORY NOT ENFORCED ON FRESH INSTALLS — migration 017 triggers silently dropped by filterForSQLite. Dogfood run 2026-08-04: fresh `consensus init` + `serve` on scratch SQLite; direct `UPDATE memory_events SET content='HACKED'` SUCCEEDED; 0 triggers in sqlite_master; schema_versions records v17 'append only memory events sqlite triggers' as applied (checksum 2cd). Root cause: filterForSQLite (internal/migrate/migrate.go) enters mTrigger skip-mode on the FIRST line of any CREATE TRIGGER that lacks ' BEGIN ' on that line, then drops every line incl. the closing one — the whole statement vanishes, runner records success. The keep-check `strings.Contains(upper, " BEGIN ")` only inspects the header line, which never contains BEGIN for multi-line triggers. README headline claim ('append-only ledger enforced by database triggers'; demo 'UPDATE attempt → 500') is FALSE on real instances; an agent with the SQL tool can rewrite its own audit trail. Postgres side also unimplemented (018 comment: 'separate task'). FIX: pass *_sqlite_* trigger files through untouched or detect BEGIN..END across lines; add post-init assertion test that triggers exist; add startup repair like repairTrustLevel.

title: [dogfood:P0] Default SQLite connection pool wedges the whole server on the documented env-var install (begin tx deadline exceeded -> API bricked until restart)
detail: Reproduced twice on fresh build at 8e3e7e6, 2026-09-09. Starting the server the README env-var way (CONSENSUS_DB_URL=sqlite:///... CONSENSUS_PORT=8124 ./consensus serve, no config file): the FIRST goal-driven session wedges the entire server. Sequence: 'harness: found active session' -> 'planning: starting interactive session' -> exactly 3m later 'harness: planning failed ... error="planning: initial context: read context: begin tx: sqlite: begin tx: context deadline exceeded"' -> heartbeat auto-retries the same session forever. During the wedged window the API first returns 401 UNAUTHENTICATED to the valid admin key, then stops answering entirely (no-auth /api/v1/health times out, HTTP 000). kill -9 -> integrity ok -> restart -> heartbeat resumes the poisoned session -> re-wedges within seconds: a session wedged this way bricks the instance on every boot (only fix is deleting the session/DB). A/B PROOF it is the pool: identical run with config-file database: { max_open_conns: 4 } executes the full loop cleanly (llm: calling provider -> response received -> commands staged -> committing -> idle). The env-var path exposes no max_open_conns override and the WAL grew to 1.5MB on a near-idle DB = pool starvation signature. Fix direction: (1) pin a safe default sqlite pool (max_open_conns<=4 or equivalent) instead of unlimited; (2) put harness transactions on a separate pool/connection class from API reads; (3) stop heartbeat-resume on a session that failed N consecutive planning windows (poison-pill guard); (4) fail loud: 'begin tx deadline' should surface as a 5xx/health-degraded event, not a silent server freeze. Evidence: /tmp/dogfood-consensus/server.log + server2.log (wedged) vs server3.log (clean), same binary.

MEASURED 2026-09-26 (live binary from HEAD): `./bin/consensus migrate down --server http://localhost:19999 --db-url sqlite:///tmp/down-trap.db` against an EMPTY db file printed 'Applied 23 migration(s): 001_initial_schema.sql ... 024_soft_delete_sessions.sql' rc=0, and sqlite3 counted 23 schema_versions rows — the opposite of rollback. ROOT CAUSE: internal/cli/migrate.go registers only create/rollback/run/version subcommands (:38-42); there is no `down` subcommand, so `migrate down` executes the parent `migrate` command whose RunE is runMigrateRun = apply-up (migrate.go:22-27,50-58; MigrateFunc('up')). The actual rollback verb is `consensus migrate rollback` (migrate.go:126-159, MigrateFunc('down') action — naming inside the code is inverted vs the CLI verbs). CONSEQUENCE: an operator following the runbook mid-incident APPLIES pending migrations when they meant to roll one back. FIX (foreman's choice): add a `down` subcommand aliasing rollback, OR correct docs/runbooks/deployment.md:74,145 (and anywhere else `migrate down` appears — grep -rn 'migrate down' docs/) to use `migrate rollback`. READER: operator. ACCEPT: `grep -rn 'migrate down' docs/` returns 0 (or `consensus migrate down` provably rolls back); the runbook's rollback command run verbatim on a scratch DB decreases the schema_versions count by 1.
worker_summary: Foreman-verified docs-only fix: deployment runbook rollback examples now use migrate rollback; grep -rn migrate down docs/ returns no matches; scratch live binary evidence confirmed migrate down applied migrations.

CONTRACT: specs/024-shim-support-matrix.md. PROVIDER SOURCES: api-docs.deepseek.com guides/anthropic_api, guides/thinking_mode, guides/tool_calls, guides/chat_prefix_completion. UPSTREAM SOURCE: sst/opencode packages/sdk/openapi.json (OpenAPI 3.1.1, the single source of truth for server + SDK generation); opencode.ai/docs/server.

title: [P2] serve with an explicit --config pointing at a nonexistent file silently boots on defaults — explicit-path miss is indistinguishable from no-config, chaos-errorpath cell UNVERIFIED twice for this class
detail: Repro (dev box, HEAD 4e92fdc3, /tmp/corrupt-test): ./consensus serve --config /nonexistent-abc.yaml starts the server (migrations applied, heartbeat loop started, rc only ends via timeout) — no error, no usage, exit never happens. Root cause: internal/config/config.go LoadWithPath treats os.IsNotExist on ANY resolved path (including the explicit SetConfigPath override wired from --config at internal/cli/serve.go:49) as 'proceed with defaults + env' (config.go:257-263). The silent-fallback contract is correct for auto-discovery (resolveConfigPath only returns paths that exist, config.go:330-337) but an operator-supplied explicit path that does not exist is silently ignored — this is exactly the missing-config behavior the QA battery's chaos-errorpath cell has now failed to pin in two consecutive cycles (QA-CONSENSUS-10, QA-CONSENSUS-17). No spec/doc text pins either behavior (specs/016-cli-interface.md §4/§8 silent on it; docs/DEBUGGING.md lists override paths without a missing-file contract), so the cell cannot grade it. Fix: when configPathOverride is explicitly set and the file is missing, return a config error (exit 1) instead of falling through to defaults; add a chaos-errorpath cell assertion once the contract is pinned. Verified live: rc=124 (timeout) with server fully booted on a nonexistent --config; battery cell chaos-errorpath INFO/UNVERIFIED with the same WARN-then-boot shape on bunker-mvp agent 49709d41.

title: [P2] session.get 404 answers the shim's own error envelope, not upstream's NamedError body - the SDK loses the server message (sdk-error-shape F1)
detail: MEASURED 2026-09-30 against pin 7945de208964a49300d7f770d1a71d078db9a4c4 (v1.18.33); pinned upstream suites = 34 ran / 32 pass / 2 fail. EXACT ASSERTION (packages/opencode/test/server/sdk-error-shape.test.ts, test 'v2 SDK error shape > 404 with NamedError body throws a real Error carrying the server message', test line 30, assertion line 44): expect(err.message).toContain("Session not found"); the same test continues at line 45 with expect(cause.status).toBe(404) and lines 46-49 with expect(cause.body).toMatchObject({name: "NotFoundError", data: {message: expect.stringContaining("Session not found")}}). FAILURE LOG EXCERPT (docs/evidence/opencode-upstream-v1.18.33/packages_opencode_test_server_sdk-error-shape_test_ts.log): 'error: expect(received).toContain(expected)' / 'Expected to contain: "Session not found"' / 'Received: "GET http://test/session/ses_no_such?directory=%2Ftmp%2Fopencode-test-684l17w2e1q -> 404 Not Found"' / '(fail) v2 SDK error shape > 404 with NamedError body throws a real Error carrying the server message [355.24ms]'. LIVE PROBE on the same revision (scratch shim, build from this tree): GET /session/ses_no_such?directory=%2Ftmp -> HTTP 404 with body {"error":{"code":"NOT_FOUND","message":"session not found"}}. The STATUS is now correct (at evidence r4 this assertion observed '401 Unauthorized', so the route/auth half has since been fixed); the defect is the BODY ENVELOPE. Upstream's SDK wrapClientError lifts data.message into Error.message only for the NamedError shape {name, data:{message}}, so with the shim's own {error:{code,message}} envelope err.message falls back to the generic fetch text and cause.body misses the shape. FIX DIRECTION: the shim already owns an upstream-shaped typed-not-found helper - writeOpencodeNotFoundError, internal/shim/opencode/server.go:1277, used for ProjectNotFoundError (internal/shim/opencode/server.go:1273) - route session.get's 404 through the upstream NamedError envelope instead of the generic /api envelope. EVIDENCE PATH: docs/evidence/opencode-upstream-v1.18.33/ (summary.md, results.tsv row 3, packages_opencode_test_server_sdk-error-shape_test_ts.log). WHY NO EXISTING ROW COVERED IT: specs/openapi/upstream/opencode-declared-vs-served-1.18.33.json lists session.get (GET /session/{sessionID}, declared 200,400,404) among 'covered' with served_outcome 200 - that comparison models path/method/status, never error-body shape, so this divergence is invisible to it and survived every prior sweep. NOT DUPLICATED: the other failing assertion in the same suite (400-class validation answered as 404 on POST /sync/history/list, SHIM-DRIFT-126) is already tracked by DF-CONSENSUS-40 and SHIM-GAP-004/SHIM-GAP-007 - see those rows rather than this one.
reasoning: WHY: this is the last thing standing between an upstream SDK client and a usable error path. The TUI catches the thrown Error and prints its .message, so a missing session currently surfaces as 'GET http://test/session/... -> 404 Not Found' instead of 'Session not found' - the exact user-facing failure the upstream test was written to prevent. It is also invisible to our own declared-vs-served grader because that grader compares routes, not response bodies, which is why it has survived every sweep to date.

title: [QA][P2][harness] ui-probe INFO is a false 'no UI' verdict on consensus: the cell's port discovery scrapes ports out of README with a docs-only ERE, so the README's stale-sidecar WORKAROUND port 8095 (pprof) enters the probe list while the documented default 8090 never does — the cell sweeps the pprof mux, collects seven 404s, and reports 'no 2xx text/html surface' for a product whose admin UI serves 200 text/html on /ui/*
reasoning:
TYPE: harness defect (battery cell false verdict) — not a product defect.
CELL: ui-probe INFO, battery tick consensus-qa-2026-10-21-08-56-31 (agent 27ce5ff6 @ dedi-2, battery HEAD 60e00577a570e8d462d05137294cb1cc82963949, evidence /tmp/bunker-qa-evidence-20261021T091608Z-2649027.jsonl, per-cell log /tmp/qa-consensus-harvest-1021/qa-logs-2713970/ui-probe.log).
CELL TEXT OBSERVED: 'go-native server answers on :8095 but NO 2xx text/html surface on any probed path [/chat /docs / /ui /dashboard /app /index.html] — exact answers: /chat=[404 text/plain; charset=utf-8] /docs=[404 ...] /=[404 ...] /ui=[404 ...] /dashboard=[404 ...] /app=[404 ...] /index.html=[404 ...] (start: go run ./cmd/consensus)'.
ROOT CAUSE (exact): bunker-qa.sh (233894 B, sha256 b2a9e1178e57e8b749e16c970f4a47d67fbec35d45b76a922876918b31d44085, commit 01c753f4f) builds UI_PORTS in the ui-probe arm as the hardcoded list '3000 5173 8000 8080 8081 8766 8767 9000 9090' PLUS ports scraped from docs: for README.md docs/reference/flags.md docs/flags.md docs/reference/cli.md it runs grep -oE '(--listen|--port|--addr|listen|port)[= :]+[^,;"]*' then grep -oE '[0-9]{4,5}'. On this repo only README.md exists, and that two-stage grep extracts exactly ONE number: 8095 — from the README's 'Port 8090 already in use? (stale sidecar shadowing)' workaround block (README.md:287 'CONSENSUS_PORT=8095 ./bin/consensus serve', :289 './bin/consensus serve --port 8095'). The documented DEFAULT port 8090 is never matched: it appears in README only as 'localhost:8090' / '-p 8090:8090' / '"8090"' / a 'CONSENSUS_PORT | 8090' table row, none of which satisfy the ERE — and 8090 is not in the hardcoded list either. So the probe list contains the WORKAROUND port instead of the default one.
WHY THAT PRODUCES A FALSE VERDICT: the arm starts the server and assigns UI_LISTEN to the first free port in UI_PORTS that answers. The started 'consensus serve' binds 127.0.0.1:8090 (api) AND 127.0.0.1:8095 (pprof debug listener — internal/config/config.go:165 default '127.0.0.1:8095'), both visible in the same ui-probe.log. 8090 is not in the probe list, 8095 is, so the cell sweeps /chat /docs / /ui /dashboard /app /index.html against the PPORF mux, which only serves /debug/pprof/* and answers net/http's default 404 for everything else — hence seven 404 text/plain answers and an INFO 'no HTML surface' verdict.

IMPACT: any Go repo whose documented default listen port is written as host:port (not as a --port flag) and which has an extra loopback listener on a docs-mentioned/other port grades ui-probe INFO — i.e. the battery reports 'no HTML surface' while the repo's UI is fully served. title: [dogfood:P1] worktree.remove does not implement the declared input contract: the declared request body {directory} is ignored and the declared ?directory=/?workspace= workspace selectors are not consulted, so on a server launched outside the repo create succeeds and remove can never succeed
reasoning: DOGFOOD 2026-10-23, real-use drive of the /experimental/worktree family merged hours earlier (ROUTE-ADD-083/084/085/086, merges ae94992/db944ae/fcb4516, HEAD 1482437), scratch sqlite instance built from HEAD, /tmp/consensus-df-1023. The upstream contract (specs/openapi/upstream/openapi-1.18.33.json) declares for DELETE /experimental/worktree: query parameters directory+workspace (optional) AND request body WorktreeRemoveInput {directory: string, required}. Two independent deviations, both A/B-proven against the same binary: (A) BODY IGNORED. Server launched IN the repo (/tmp/consensus-df-1023/proj, port 18392): DELETE with the declared body only {"directory":"<linked worktree>"} -> 400 WorktreeRemoveFailedError "worktree.remove needs an explicit directory query parameter"; the identical request with ?directory=<linked worktree> and no body -> 200 true and the worktree really disappeared from disk and from `git worktree list`. The body is never read; only the query parameter is. The sibling reset handler is the opposite (DELETE-style body-less reset -> 400 InvalidRequestError kind=Body, body required), so the family is internally inconsistent: one op demands the declared body, the other silently ignores it. Provider: internal/shim/opencode/experimental_worktree_list_remove.go (handleExperimentalWorktreeRemove) reads only q.Get("directory") as the target. (B) DECLARED WORKSPACE SELECTORS IGNORED. Server launched OUTSIDE the repo (cwd /tmp/consensus-df-1023, port 18391 — the realistic case, e.g. a systemd unit with no WorkingDirectory): POST /experimental/worktree?directory=<repo> -> 200 and a real git worktree on disk (create DOES honour the declared selector, via worktreeCreateDeclaredDirectory, experimental_worktree_create.go:229-240); GET /experimental/worktree?directory=<repo> -> 200 listing it; then DELETE /experimental/worktree?directory=<that worktree> -> 400 WorktreeNotGitError "workspace /tmp/consensus-df-1023 is not a git repository: exit status 128", and reset -> 400 the same way. Cause: remove/reset take the workspace from apiV2LocationSelector (api_v2_lists.go:87-111), which reads only the bracketed location[directory]/location[workspace] selectors and otherwise falls back to requestWorkspaceDir -> header x-opencode-directory or the process CWD (server.go:3645-3665). SPEC-017 §3.10 pins the resolution order for the shim workspace as "x-opencode-directory, then the declared ?directory= selector, then ?workspace=, then the configured workdir" — the middle two are absent here, and worktree.remove/reset are the only handlers in the family that skip them. Workarounds proven live (both 200 true, worktree removed): add header x-opencode-directory=<repo>, or send ?location[directory]=<repo>. Net user impact: a client that creates a worktree (create honours ?directory=) can never remove it unless the server happened to be started inside the repo, so worktrees accumulate on disk; the failure message names an unrelated directory, which reads as a server fault rather than a selector problem. FIX DIRECTION: take the removal target from the declared body (WorktreeRemoveInput.directory) with the query parameter as an accepted alternative, and resolve the workspace in the SPEC-017 order for remove+reset so all four handlers agree. EVIDENCE: /tmp/consensus-df-1023/evidence (arm logs), full arms in docs/dogfood/2026-10-23-worktree-copy-surface.md, dogfood-log 2026-10-23 entry.

title: [P1] Documented Docker run path cannot start: the image exits 1 with sqlite 'unable to open database file (14)' because the VOLUME mount point /home/consensus/data is created root:root while the process runs uid 1000 — 'docker run -p 8090:8090 consensus' and README Option 2 both read health 000

battery.head: bad2397c0bce96e30198a9fedf899c86d4b5c8b2
battery.note: the battery's docker-deploy and chaos-shutdown cells were SKIPPED by the controller lifecycle safety gate, so no cell covered this path; the docker-build stage was run off-battery at the same head (docker build rc=0) and the image was then exercised by hand

detail.reproduced_on: dev box (controller), docker 29.1.3; image built from HEAD: docker build -t consensus-qa:bad2397 . -> rc=0
repro_verbatim: docker volume rm consensus-qa-readme-vol; docker run -d --name consensus-qa-readme -p 18099:8090 -v consensus-qa-readme-vol:/home/consensus/data -e DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-dummy-not-real consensus-qa:bad2397
docker logs consensus-qa-readme (tail): db: driver: sqlite backend failed: sqlite: ping failed: unable to open database file (14)
detail.root_cause: Dockerfile:27-29 adduser + USER consensus + WORKDIR /home/consensus, then Dockerfile:37 declares VOLUME ["/home/consensus/data"] without ever creating or chowning that directory (no mkdir/chown layer). Docker materialises a fresh volume mount point root:root 0755 while the process runs uid 1000: 'ls -ld /home/consensus/data' -> drwxr-xr-x root root; 'id' -> uid=1000(consensus). The default DB path (Dockerfile:39 and CMD:45, CONSENSUS_DB_URL=sqlite:///home/consensus/data/consensus.db) therefore cannot be created and the server exits before binding.
controls: same path writable -> starts: --tmpfs /home/consensus/data -> /api/v1/health 200 ('api: starting addr=0.0.0.0:8090'); host dir 0777 bind-mounted at /home/consensus/data -> /api/v1/health 200
Dockerfile header's Prod line shape '-v consensus-data:/data' -> still exits; it also points at the wrong path (the DB lives in /home/consensus/data)
reproduced twice (dummy DEEPSEEK_API_KEY set as README does; and keyless) — identical exit 1
detail.impact: Every documented sqlite container run fails: Dockerfile:3 'docker run -p 8090:8090 consensus' (anonymous root-owned volume), README Option 2 'docker run -d --name consensus -p 8090:8090 -v consensus-data:/home/consensus/data ...' (named volume), and the Dockerfile header's '-v consensus-data:/data' prod line. The observable symptom is the health probe reading 000 — the same shape QA-CONSENSUS-8/16 recorded from the battery's docker probe, now with a root cause. docker-compose.prod.yml pins PostgreSQL for the app so it does not take the sqlite path, but it mounts the same consensus-data:/home/consensus/data volume, so anything the process writes there inherits the same permission shape.
detail.fix: Dockerfile: create and own the data directory before switching user, e.g. RUN mkdir -p /home/consensus/data && chown -R consensus:consensus /home/consensus/data in the same layer as adduser (before USER consensus); align the header's Prod volume path with CONSENSUS_DB_URL (/home/consensus/data, not /data).
detail.dedupe: distinct from QA-CONSENSUS-8/16 (dev compose starts only the Postgres dependency so the app port never answers, plus the deploy-surface contract). This row is 'the image starts but the app cannot open its own default sqlite path'.

reasoning: Clean-machine deploy path: the image is the one CI publishes and the README documents; it builds green and then cannot start under its own default run command. Found because the battery's docker cells were gated off this tick, so the docker-build stage was run off-battery and the resulting image was executed by hand (README Option 2 shape, then controls).
review_notes: Fix is a two-line Dockerfile change (mkdir+chown before USER, and correct the header's -v path). Verify by running the README command shape on a clean host and reading health 200; also confirm 'ls -ld /home/consensus/data' inside the container reports uid 1000.

cells_verbatim.ui-probe: INFO — 'go-native start command is not a long-running server (rc/exit in log) — no HTML surface to probe: consensus: startup failed: LLM API key not configured (set DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, CONSENSUS_API_KEY, or set llm.provider=mock); ... exit status 1 (repo declares default port(s) 8090 8767)'
